text:
A natural number has prime factorization given by $n = 2^{x}3^{y}5^{z}$, where y and z are such 
that y + z = 5 and $y^{-1} + z^{-1} =$ $\frac{5}{6}$, y > z. Then the number of odd divisors of n, including 1, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
y + z = 5 ....... (1)

$\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y+z}{yz}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{yz}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ yz = 6

Also, (y $-$ $z)^{2} = (y + z)^{2}$ $-$ 4yz

$\Rightarrow$ (y $-$ $z)^{2} = (y + z)^{2}$ $-$ 4yz

$\Rightarrow$ (y $-$ $z)^{2} = 25$ $-$ 4(6) = 1

$\Rightarrow$ y $-$ z = 1 ..... (2)

from (1) and (2), y = 3 and z = 2

for calculating odd divisor of $p = 2^{x} . 3^{y} . 5^{z}$

x must be zero

$P = 2^{0} . 3^{3} . 5^{2}$ 

$\Rightarrow$ Total possible cases $= (3^{0}5^{0} + 3^{1}5^{0} + 3^{2}5^{0} + 3^{3}5^{0} + .... + 3^{3}5^{2})$

$\therefore$ Total odd divisors must be (3 + 1) ( 2 + 1) = 12

$=\log _{e}(1+a)+\log _{e}(1+b)$

text: Let $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}e^{t}f(t)dt+e^{x}$ be a differentiable function for all x$\in$R. Then f(x) equals :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x}e^{t}f(t)dt+e^{x}$ .... (1)

Differentiating both sides w.r.t. x

$f^{'}(x)=e^{x}.f(x)+e^{x}$ (Using Newton-Leibnitz Theorem)

$\Rightarrow \frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)+1}=e^{x}$

Integrating w.r.t. x

$\int \frac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)+1}dx=\int e^{x}dx$

$\Rightarrow \ln (f(x)+1)=e^{x}+c$

Put x = 0

ln 2 = 1 + c ($\because$ f(0) = 1, from equation (1))

$\therefore$ $\ln (f(x)+1)=e^{x}+\ln 2-1$

$\Rightarrow f(x)+1=2.e^{e^{x}-1}$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=2e^{e^{x}-1}-1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text: For x > 0, if $f(x)=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\log _{e}t}{(1+t)}dt$, then $f(e)+f\left (\frac{1}{e}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\ln t}{1+t}dt$

then $f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\int\limits _{1}^{1/x}\frac{\ln t}{1+t}dt$

Let $t=\frac{1}{u}\Rightarrow dt=-\frac{1}{u^{2}}du$

$\Rightarrow f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\ln \frac{1}{u}}{1+\frac{1}{u}}\left (-\frac{1}{u^{2}}\right )dx$

$f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\ln u}{u(1+u)}du=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\ln t}{t(1+t)}dt$

$\therefore$ $f(x)+f\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\ln t\left (\frac{1}{1+t}+\frac{1}{t(1+t)}\right )dt$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\ln t\left (\frac{1}{1+t}+\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t+1}\right )dt$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{x}\frac{\ln t}{t}dt=\frac{1}{2}(\ln x)^{2}$

$\therefore$ $f(e)+f\left (\frac{1}{e}\right )=\frac{1}{2}(\ln e)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

$\Rightarrow 4x^{2}-12x+9+4y^{2}-8y+4=1$

text: If vectors $\vec{a_{1}}=x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{a_{2}}=\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$ are collinear, then a possible unit vector parallel to the vector $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a_{2}}=λ\vec{a_{1}}$

$\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}=λ(x\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k})$

$1=λx,y=-λ,z=λ$

$x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}=\frac{1}{λ}\hat{i}-λ\hat{j}+λ\widehat{k}$

Unit vector $=\frac{\frac{1}{λ}\hat{i}-λ\hat{j}+λ\widehat{k}}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{λ2}+λ^{2}+λ^{2}}}$

$=\frac{\hat{i}-λ^{2}\hat{j}+λ^{2}\widehat{k}}{\sqrt{1+2λ^{4}}}$

Let $λ^{2}=1$, possible unit vector $=\frac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\widehat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}$

text:
If the matrix $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$ satisfies the equation

 $A^{20}+αA^{19}+βA=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ for some real numbers $α$ and $β$, then $β$ $-$ $α$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{3}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 16 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\begin{array}{ll}  & . \\  & . \\  & . \\  & . \\  & . \\  & . \end{array}$

$A^{19}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2^{19} & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right ],A^{20}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2^{20} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$L.H.S.=A^{20}+αA^{19}+βA=$

$\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1+α+β & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2^{20}+α2^{19}+2β & 0 \\ 3α+3β & 0 & 1-α-β \end{array}\right ]$

$R.H.S.=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow α+β=0$ and $2^{20}+α2^{19}+2β=4$

$\Rightarrow 2^{20}+α(2^{19}-2)=4$

$\Rightarrow α=\frac{4-2^{20}}{2^{19}-2}=-2$

$\Rightarrow β=2$

$\therefore$ $β-α=4$

text: Let $α$ and $β$ be two real numbers such that $α$ + $β$ = 1 and $αβ$ = $-$1. Let $p_{n} = (α)^{n} + (β)^{n}, p_{n-1} = 11$ and $p_{n+1} = 29$ for some integer n $\geq$ 1. Then, the value of p${}_{n}^{2}$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $α$ + $β$ = 1, $αβ$ = $-$ 1

$\therefore$ Quadratic equation with roots $α$, $β$ is $x^{2}$ $-$ x $-$ 1 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $α^{2}$ = $α$ + 1

Multiplying both sides by $α^{n-1}$

$α^{n+1}$ = $α^{n}$ + $α^{n-1}$ ......(1)

Similarly,

$β^{n + 1}$ = $β^{n}$ + $β^{n - 1}$ ..... (2)

Adding (1) & (2)

$α^{n+1}+β^{n+1}=(α^{n}+β^{n})+(α^{n-1}+β^{n-1})$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{n+1} = P_{n} + P_{n-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $29 = P_{n} + 11 ($Given, $P_{n + 1} = 29, P_{n - 1} = 11)$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{n} = 18$

$\therefore$ $P_{n}^{2}$ $= 18^{2} = 324$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text:
Let z be those complex numbers which satisfy

| z + 5 | $\leq$ 4 and z(1 + i) + $z–$(1 $-$ i) $\geq$ $-$10, i = $\sqrt{-1}$.

If the maximum value of $| z + 1 |^{2}$ is $α$ + $β\sqrt{2}$, then the value of ($α$ + $β$) is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, z = x + iy

Given, z(1 + i) + $z–$ (1 $-$ i) $\geq$ $-$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ z + $z–$ + i (z $-$ $z–$) $\geq$ $-$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ 2x + i (2iy) $\geq$ $-$ 10

$\Rightarrow$ $x + i^{2} y$ $\geq$ $-$ 5

$\Rightarrow$ x $-$ y $\geq$ $-$ 5 ...... (1)

Also given, | z + 5 | $\leq$ 4

$\Rightarrow$ | z $-$ ($-$5 + 0i) | $\leq$ 4 ...... (2)

It represents a circle whose center at ($-$ 5, 0) and radius 4. z is inside of the circle.

[IMG]


From (1) and (2) z is the shaded region of the diagram.

Now, | z + 1 | = | z $-$ ($-$1 + 0 i) | = distance of z from ($-$1, 0).

Clearly 'p' is the required position of 'z' when | z + 1 | is maximum.

$\therefore$ P $\equiv$ ($-$5 $-$ 4 cos45${}^{\circ }$, 0 $-$ 4sin45${}^{\circ }$) = ($-$5$-$2$\sqrt{2}$, $-$2$\sqrt{2}$)

$\therefore$ $(PQ)^{2}|_{\max } = 32 + 16\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = 32

$\Rightarrow$ $β$ = 16

Thus, $α$ + $β$ = 48

text:
If the arithmetic mean and geometric mean of the $p^{th}$ and $q^{th}$ terms of the 
sequence $-$16, 8, $-$4, 2, ...... satisfy the equation
 $4x^{2}$ $-$ 9x + 5 = 0, then p + q is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $4x^{2}-9x+5=0$

$\Rightarrow (x-1)(4x-5)=0$

$\Rightarrow$ A. M. $=\frac{5}{4}$, G. M. = 1 (As A. M. $\geq$ G. M)

Again, for the series

$-$16, 8, $-$4, 2 ..........

$p^{th}$ term $t_{p}=-16\left (\frac{-1}{2}\right )^{p-1}$

$q^{th}$ term $t_{p}=16\left (\frac{-1}{2}\right )^{q-1}$

Now, A. M. = $\frac{t_{p}+t_{q}}{2}=\frac{5}{4}$ & G. M. = $\sqrt{t_{p}t_{q}}=1$

$\Rightarrow 16^{2}\left (-\frac{1}{2}\right )^{p+q-2}=1$

$\Rightarrow (-2)^{8}=(-2)^{(p+q-2)}$

$\Rightarrow p+q=10$

text:
If $I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{m-1}(1-x)^{n-1}dx$, for m, $n\geq 1$, and 
$\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{x^{m-1}+x^{n-1}}{(1+x)^{m+n}}dx=αI_{m,n}α\in R$, then $α$ equals $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{m-1}.(1-x)^{n-1}dx$

Put $x=\frac{1}{y+1}\Rightarrow dx=\frac{-1}{(y+1)^{2}}dy$

$1-x=\frac{y}{y+1}$

$\therefore$ $I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{\infty }^{0}\frac{y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}(-1)dy=\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\frac{y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy$ .... (i)

Similarly, $I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{n-1}.(1-x)^{m-1}dx$

$\Rightarrow I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\frac{y^{m-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy$ .... (ii)

From (i) & (ii)

$2I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{\infty }\frac{y^{m-1}+y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy$

$\Rightarrow 2I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{y^{m-1}+y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy+\int\limits _{1}^{\infty }\frac{y^{m-1}+y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy=I_{1}+I_{2}$

Put $y=\frac{1}{z}$ in $I_{2}$

$dy=-\frac{1}{z^{2}}dz$

$\Rightarrow 2I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{y^{m-1}+y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy+\int\limits _{1}^{0}\frac{z^{m-1}+z^{n-1}}{(z+1)^{m+n}}(-dz)$

$\Rightarrow I_{m,n}=\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{y^{m-1}+y^{n-1}}{(y+1)^{m+n}}dy\Rightarrow α=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift

text:
Let $X_{1}, X_{2}, ......., X_{18}$ be eighteen observations such 
that $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{18}(X_{i}-α)=36$ and $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{18}(X_{i}-β)^{2}=90$, where $α$ and $β$ are distinct real numbers. If the standard deviation of these observations is 1, then the value of | $α$ $-$ $β$ | is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{18}(x_{1}-α)=36$

$\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}-18α=36$

$\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}=18(α+2)$ .... (1)

Also, $\sum\limits _{i=1}^{18}(x_{1}-β)^{2}=90$

$\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}+18β^{2}-2β\sum x_{i}=90$

$\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}+18β^{2}+2β\times 18(α+2)=90$ (using equation (1))

$\Rightarrow \sum x_{i}^{2}=90-18β^{2}+36β(α+2)$

Given, $σ^{2}=1\Rightarrow \frac{1}{18}\sum x_{i}^{2}-\left (\frac{\sum x_{i}}{18}\right )^{2}=1$

$=\frac{1}{18}(90-18β^{2}+36αβ+72β)-\left (\frac{18(α+2)}{18}\right )^{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow 90-18β^{2}+36αβ+72β-18(α+2)^{2}=18$

$\Rightarrow 5-β^{2}+2αβ+4β-(α+2)^{2}=1$

$\Rightarrow 5-β^{2}+2αβ+4β-α^{2}-4-4α=1$

$\Rightarrow α^{2}-β^{2}+2αβ+4β-4α=0$

$\Rightarrow (α-β)(α-β+4)=0$

$\Rightarrow α-β=-4$

$\therefore$ $|α-β|=4$ $(α\neq β)$

text:
Let a be an integer such that all the real roots of the polynomial 
$2x^{5} + 5x^{4} + 10x^{3} + 10x^{2} + 10x + 10$ lie in the interval (a, a + 1). Then, |a| is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let, $f(x)=2x^{5}+5x^{4}+10x^{3}+10x^{2}+10x+10$

$\Rightarrow f^{'}(x)=10(x^{4}+2x^{3}+3x^{2}+2x+1)$

$=10\left (x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}+2\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+3\right )$

$=10\left (\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2}+2\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+1\right )$

$=10\left (\left (x+\frac{1}{x}\right )+1\right )^{2}>0;\forall x\in R$

$\therefore$ f(x) is strictly increasing function. Since, it is an odd degree polynomial it will have exactly one real root.

Now, by observation.

$f(-1)=3>0$

$f(-2)=-64+80-80+40-20+10$

$=-34<0$

$\Rightarrow f(x)$ has at least one root in $(-2,-1)\equiv (a,a+1)$

$\Rightarrow a=-2$

$\Rightarrow$ |a| = 2
